newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Mobil PDVSA sign $2.3bln crude upgrade deal.
newsitem.headline: Mobil PDVSA sign $2.3bln crude upgrade deal.

text.p: Mobil Oil Corporation signed Tuesday a $2.3 billion deal to upgrade and sell heavy Venezuelan crude with Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) subsidiary Lagoven, Lagoven President Julius Trinkunas said.
Under the project, the joint venture will produce, upgrade and sell about 100,000 barrels per day (bpd) of extra heavy crude from the Cerro Negro area of Venezuela's Orinoco Tar Belt.
The project, which will create a 35 year joint venture, will be presented to Venezuela's Congress before the end of the year for final approval, Trinkunas said.
Heavy crude of eight degrees API (American Petroleum Institute) will be upgraded to 16 degree API at a plant in Jose on Venezuela's Caribbean coast.
The semi-finished product will be moved to Mobil's 170,000 barrel per day (bpd) Chalmette, Louisiana refinery where the processing will be completed.
Lagoven and Mobil hope to market the finished synthetic crude on the U.S. Gulf Coast and East Coast markets, Trinkunas said.

"We are very pleased and enthusiastic about forming this partnership with Lagoven. We believe that it is the start of a long and fruitful relationship," Mobil executive vice president Robert Swanson said.

Mobil also controls controls 50 percent of a lubricants plant in Venezuela. The company recently started exploration work for light and medium crudes in western Venezuela under a profit sharing agreement in partnership with Germany's Veba Oel AG and Japan's Nippon Oil Co Ltd.
The crude upgrade scheme signed Tuesday is one of several projects designed to take advantage of Venezuela's vast extra- heavy crude reserves in the Orinoco Tar Belt.
PDVSA unit Corpoven recently signed a $3.5 billion deal with Atlantic Richfield Co to upgrade and market 197,000 bpd of crude from the tar belt.
